subject: Onyx Health pilot — minimum egress & residency checklist
messages:
From: Emily Su <emily.su@onyxhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Oliver Chang <oliver.chang@onyxhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onyx pilot — follow-up and list of data/egress asks

Hi Rachel / Oliver,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the session was helpful. A couple quick items we need to lock down before the pilot:

- PII scope: we will definitely be sending names, email addresses and small clinical notes (no full PHI PDFs for the pilot). We need confirmation on how Redwood handles PII in the request lifecycle (in-flight, cache/KV, and any logs).
- Retention: target for pilot is API request payloads dropped after 30 days; audit logs retained 90 days but must be exportable on demand.
- Minimal egress: Onyx security wants zero internet egress from our VPC other than allowed AWS endpoints under customer control (S3 for artifacts, KMS for CMKs). No telemetry to third-party analytics.
- Logging: we’d prefer logs (access/audit) pushed to our SIEM over TLS (syslog or HTTPS ingest) rather than stored on Redwood-managed long-term buckets.
- Air-gap: not required for pilot, but we need clear guidance if we escalate to on-prem in Q3.

Can you send a one-page checklist we can circulate to our security team plus a minimal network port/IP list we can give infra? Happy to share our internal network diagram if helpful.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Su
Head of Platform Security, Onyx Health
emily.su@onyxhealth.com

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Onyx pilot — follow-up and list of data/egress asks

Team — forwarding Emily’s list. Quick proposal for what we can commit for the pilot and what we need from Onyx:

Commit (pilot scope):
- Private/VPC deployment in us-east-1 (customer VPC peering or dedicated subnet in our infra) with model serving confined to the VPC.
- No outbound internet access from the runtime nodes except to customer-authorized endpoints (S3, KMS, and optionally an internal SIEM endpoint).
- Ephemeral KV/cache retention: default 30 days for persisted request artifacts; we can set TTLs to shorter values for the pilot.
- Audit logs: retain 90 days on our side and provide an automated export to Onyx S3 or push to their SIEM.

What we need from Onyx:
- Internal network diagram showing NAT/firewall rules and the intended egress target(s) (S3 endpoints, SIEM ingest URL, KMS key ARNs).
- Confirmation of exact retention window and any regulatory constraints (e.g., specific region residency).
- Contact for infra (IP allowlist / firewall owner).

Diego — can you draft the minimal port/IP list and a short network diagram template?
Soojin — can you confirm retention/elog SLAs we can promise for a pilot and options for stricter retention if they move to on-prem?

I’m attaching the draft pilot requirements and the Redwood security summary (short). I’ll send Emily a one-page checklist once we have Diego’s ports.

Attachments: onyx_pilot_mvp_requirements.pdf, redwood_security_summary.pdf

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Onyx pilot — follow-up and list of data/egress asks

Rachel / Soojin,

Draft port / egress guidance for the checklist (pilot minimum):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from runtime subnets to:
  - internal model LB (private IPs / internal ALB) in Redwood-managed VPC / peered VPC (we can exchange CIDR ranges).
  - customer S3 endpoints (via VPC endpoints / gateway endpoints) — prefer VPC endpoint so no NAT traversal.
  - customer KMS endpoint (regional).
  - SIEM ingest host(s): customer-provided FQDNs/IPs (TLS only).
- Block all other outbound IP ranges by default.
- No DNS resolution allowed to non-authorized domains; DNS requests should go to customer-provided resolvers.

Operational notes:
- KV cache is ephemeral and kept in-memory where feasible; any persisted artifacts are written to customer S3 or short-lived Redwood-managed storage with TTL enforced.
- For audit logs, we can push via HTTPS to Onyx SIEM with mutual TLS (mTLS) or write to a customer S3 bucket using a cross-account role.
- If Onyx requests air-gap/on-prem later, we’ll need an additional security review and a separate deployment plan (timeline ~6–8 weeks).

I’ll draft a simple two-box network diagram (Redwood runtime <-> VPC peering <-> Onyx infra) and share the PNG by EOD.

- Diego
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Su <emily.su@onyxhealth.com>, Oliver Chang <oliver.chang@onyxhealth.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onyx pilot — follow-up and list of data/egress asks

Hi Emily / Oliver — thanks for the clear asks. Short checklist attached and answers inline below. Copying Diego and Soojin.

Pilot commitments (what Redwood will provide):
- Deployment: Private deployment option in us-east-1; we will run model-serving inside a dedicated VPC/subnet with peering to Onyx or via customer-managed Transit Gateway.
- Egress control: No general internet egress from runtime nodes. Allowed egress is restricted to:
  * Customer-owned S3 endpoints (via VPC endpoint)
  * Customer KMS (regional)
  * Customer SIEM ingest endpoints over TLS (mTLS available)
- Data residency: Pilot data will reside in us-east-1. If Onyx requires EU residency later we can arrange region specific deployment.
- Retention: Default pilot settings — request artifacts dropped after 30 days; audit logs retained 90 days. We can shorten the request artifact TTL to match stricter policies for the pilot on request.
- Logging: Option A — push logs to Onyx SIEM over TLS (recommended). Option B — write encrypted audit exports to a customer S3 bucket with cross-account role.

What we need from Onyx to finalize the checklist:
1) Network diagram with NAT/firewall owners and intended egress targets (S3/KMS/SIEM).
2) Exact retention windows you want enforced for request artifacts and for logs.
3) Point of contact to provide IPs/FQDNs for SIEM ingestion.

Attachments included: onyx_pilot_mvp_requirements.pdf (pilot scope and MAD), redwood_security_summary.pdf (summary of relevant controls).

Next steps:
- Please upload your network diagram to the shared Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_onx_pilot_design
- I’ll set a 30-minute sync for Wed Mar 31 to walk the diagram and confirm egress ACLs / retention.
- If you want a written Mutual Action Plan I can circulate the draft and include dates for the pilot kickoff.

If anything above is a showstopper (e.g., absolute ban on any third-party TLS endpoints) call that out and we’ll escalate.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: onyx_pilot_mvp_requirements.pdf (attached), redwood_security_summary.pdf (attached)
